accepted_claims.claim: Donnayite identity and reassigned type collection
accepted_claims.support: Six of seven catalogued cotype specimens are alicewilsonite-(YCe); CMNMC 39396 becomes donnayite holotype under approved proposal 22-F.
17 microprobe analyses, Y2O3 mean 10.18 wt%; 20 kV, 10 nA, 30 micrometre beam; stoichiometric CO2/H2O, not direct measurements.
Holotype R1 .139 unsuccessful model; CMNMC 90405 yielded P1 model at 293 K, R1 .055 for 3366 observed reflections. Split sites, proxies and unlocated H qualify model.

limits: Original 1978 article was not separately acquired. Its historical conflation is accepted only as the 2023 investigators' reassessment, not an independent reread of 1978 measurements.
Table 5 Rint .092 versus official CIF equivalent-reflection agreement .0342 remains unresolved; do not choose a preferred number for downstream quantitative comparison.
CSD 2223388 is reported by the article but was not independently resolved through ICSD; no extra accession is asserted.
Part 1 Table 8 lists Mont Saint-Hilaire for alicewilsonite-(YLa), whereas its introduction and current IMA indicate Australia. That other-species locality is excluded from accepted owners.

sources.title: Mckelveyite group minerals – Part 2: Alicewilsonite-(YCe), Na2Sr2YCe(CO3)6·3H2O, a new species
sources.inspection: Complete 13-page text; all Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–6 visually checked. Official CIF identity, formula, cell, occupancies, hydrogen/quality replies and refinement fields checked; full powder-pattern numeric shape checked. No independent diffraction refinement.

accepted_claims.locator: p.143 introduction and p.145 nomenclature; IMA 2026 p.6
accepted_claims.support: IMA 2020-055, holotype CMNMC 53660. Y and Ce distinguish different sites; no elemental-commodity equivalence.

Zoned crystal, Alice outer rim versus Donnayite/gaidonnayite inner assemblage; diffraction grain selected from Alice rim. Six microprobe analyses give Y2O3 8.52 wt%, Ce2O3 9.52 wt%; volatiles calculated and infrared water support qualitative.
P1, 293 K, R1 .055, 3753 observed reflections, 87:13 twin model. Poor crystal quality, omitted Ca, Ce/Dy scattering proxies and unlocated hydrogen limit exact model chemistry.

limits: Sr1 prose p.150 uses Sr.73Ce.23Ba.05 but Table 4 and CIF use Sr.73Ce.22Ba.05; the discrepancy is retained, not silently normalized.

Table 3 Rint .062 differs from .0394 in the CIF equivalent-reflection field; .0394 also appears after 4117 in the table unique-reflections cell. Underlying definitions/processing versions need clarification.
Table 6 Donnayite peak d 3.025 differs from Part 1 Table 4 d 3.052. This comparative number is excluded; it does not change accepted species separation.
Figure 2 caption describes partial replacement by gaidonnayite while prose qualifies possible replacement; no time-resolved controlled transformation is established.
p.148 HCl dissolution with effervescence at room temperature lacks concentration, time, loading and yield; no structured extraction/recovery mechanism accepted.
Natural epitaxy occurs in both directions at Mont Saint-Hilaire, with no consistent genetic trend. Proposed high-temperature disordered polymorphism is not observed experimental conversion.
